title: BOTANICAL CERAMIDE AND BARRIER-LIPID SCIENCE F106-F110 | Family 22 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch  |  33 x STARLI  |  Edition v1.0 / November 2026 A companion to the 819-page integrated research atlas: botanical-active/ceramide precipitation, three-lipid mole-fraction order, lamellar repeat spacing, spatial delivery and viable-model water-loss evidence. Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Traditional materia-medica scholarship is used as a source of research questions, not as a substitute for evidence of human tolerance or cosmetic efficacy. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F106-F110; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of authenticated botanical, lamellar and barrier evidence F106 - Botanical Active-Ceramide Compatibility at the Limit: primary endpoint botanical-active / ceramide precipitation fraction (%). Fair comparator: full-lipid reference, active-only, ceramide-only, matched vehicle and equal-oil nonlamellar controls. Disqualifying counterexample: color/turbidity interference, precipitated cholesterol, pH-triggered crystal formation, non-specific surface adsorption, pigment scattering. F107 - Ceramide-Cholesterol-Fatty Acid Ratios at the Limit: primary endpoint lamellar-order parameter (dimensionless) under defined three-lipid mole ratios. Fair comparator: matched single-lipid omissions, equimass nonlamellar dispersions and same-total-lipid reference. Disqualifying counterexample: bulk lipid crystallization masquerading as lamellar order, peak overlap, crystal orientation and off-ratio total-solids change. F108 - Botanical Lipid Lamellar Structure Formation at the Limit: primary endpoint lamellar-domain repeat spacing (nm) with reported scattering resolution. Fair comparator: equal-total-lipid disordered reference, reordered lipid mixture and water-activity-matched blank. Disqualifying counterexample: instrument q-calibration drift, sample thickness, cholesterol crystals, preferred orientation or hydration swelling misassigned to layered structure. F109 - Botanical Barrier Lipid Nanodelivery at the Limit: primary endpoint coefficient of variation of component distribution in a nonclinical lipid model (%). Fair comparator: equal-lipid nonlamellar vehicle, matched blank nanocarrier, free-active mixture and depth-attenuation reference. Disqualifying counterexample: fluorescent dye decoupling, light attenuation, optical scatter, surface contamination mistaken for depth deposition. F110 - Barrier Recovery Evidence for Botanical-Ceramide Blends at the Limit: primary endpoint qualified nonclinical water-loss flux (g/m2/h), with independent RhE viability (%). Fair comparator: equal-lipid vehicle, occlusive inert reference, missing-ceramide arm, full-lipid reference and sham-treated qualified RhE. Disqualifying counterexample: temporary occlusive masking, chamber acclimation, humidity drift, damaged or nonviable tissue, incomplete evaporation correction.

BOTANICAL POLYSACCHARIDE HYDRATION SCIENCE F101-F105 | Family 21 | Civilizational Scientific Research Notebook White Rainbow Epoch  |  33 x STARLI  |  Edition v1.0 / November 2026 A companion to the 819-page integrated research atlas: molecular-weight sorption, glycerol co-hydration, hyaluronan rheology, surface-film mass, and long-time water-loss evidence. Editorial scope and safety boundary This is a prospective research design, not a report of completed experiments. The graphical response surfaces are synthetic and reproducible. Traditional materia-medica scholarship is used as a source of research questions, not as a substitute for evidence of human tolerance or cosmetic efficacy. Source-lineage and the native endpoints are inherited from the 817-page STARLI Master Blueprint F101-F105; the narrative and candidate models are newly elaborated research proposals. A five-part chain of polysaccharide-hydration-botanical causation F101 - Botanical Polysaccharide Molecular Weight and Water Uptake at the Limit: primary endpoint equilibrium water uptake ratio (g water/g dry polysaccharide). Fair comparator: mass-matched glycerol, hyaluronan alone, vehicle blank and equal-solids polysaccharide fractions. Disqualifying counterexample: residual free glycerol or salt, transient osmotic absorption, aggregation, poor dry-mass calibration and evaporation artefact masquerading as equilibrium binding. F102 - Botanical Polysaccharide-Glycerol Hydration Coupling at the Limit: primary endpoint glycerol–polysaccharide nonadditive water-uptake interaction (g/g). Fair comparator: polysaccharide alone, glycerol alone, vehicle and equal-total-solids noninteracting mixture references. Disqualifying counterexample: differing total solids, vehicle evaporation, non-equilibrated glycerol osmotic draw, tissue occlusion and unequal humidity. F103 - Botanical Polysaccharide-Hyaluronan Compatibility at the Limit: primary endpoint hyaluronan-blend viscosity drift (Pa.s at specified shear rate and temperature). Fair comparator: hyaluronan-only, polysaccharide-only, equal-solids noninteracting reference and order-reversed mixing. Disqualifying counterexample: pH and ionic-strength mismatches, shear-induced degradation, chain entanglement relaxation or sedimentation falsely described as molecular synergy. F104 - Botanical Polysaccharide Moisture-Film Formation at the Limit: primary endpoint recoverable surface moisture-film mass (mg/cm2). Fair comparator: equal-solids vehicle, glycerol-only film, hyaluronan-only film, blank carrier and pre-rinsed surface. Disqualifying counterexample: unrecovered substrate water, transient wetting, probe films mistaken for absorbed material, optical contrast or uneven local film coverage. F105 - Long-Duration Hydration Evidence for Botanical Polysaccharide Blends at the Limit: primary endpoint time-integral of cumulative surface water loss (g.h/m2; specified interval). Fair comparator: mass-matched glycerol, hyaluronan single ingredients, equal-solids vehicle, occlusive reference and baseline-adjusted untreated model. Disqualifying counterexample: temporary osmotic uptake followed by rebound evaporation, chamber climate drift, surface occlusion, nonviable tissue and sensor acclimation bias.
